item: How large the open island is
help: "standard": 600 px wide, its pages 150 px tall. "large": 720 px wide and every page 210 px tall, each laid out for the room (a larger cover, timer ring and month, more rows and cards); the type keeps its size.

item: The day beside the closed island's clock
help: "Fri 6" before the time while the island shows the clock alone.
system: as GNOME's own clock is set. 24h: 20:40. 12h: 8:40 PM, with AM or PM. Every time Island shows follows it.
With the Glass look: how dark the glass is, from 0 (clear, what is behind shows through) to 100 (dark frosted glass). Still blurred either way.
How black the top bar beside the island is, in %: 0 is glass, 100 is black and the island blends into it. Unset, top-bar-style decides.

With a see-through or grey top bar: while an app's window reaches the bar (maximized, tiled to the top or moved up there), the bar turns black, so the wallpaper doesn't show above it. The island stays where it is.
Smaller text and spacing in the top bar; with the island below the bar, a slimmer bar too.

"notch": joined to the top of the screen, its shoulders flaring into it. "pill": floating free, round all over, a little below the top: centred in the top bar with the closed island inside it, else just below the bar, or 8 px from the top of a display without one.

item: Closed island inside the top bar
help: Like a notch: the top bar is as tall as the closed island (plus the space below it), so it never covers windows. Alerts and the open island still hang below it for a moment.
From LRCLIB, by the song's title, artist and length.
"hover": when the pointer rests on it. "click": only when clicked.

item: How long the pointer rests before the island opens, in milliseconds

help: off: always shown. always: hides once the pointer has been off it a while. top-bar: hides and comes back with a top bar another extension hides. windows: hides while an app's window reaches the top (maximized, tiled or moved up there). Hidden, alerts, the open island and the assistant still show; pointing at its place in the top bar brings it back.

item: How long the closed island waits before hiding, in seconds

help: When on, alerts (notifications, calls, timers…) show over a full-screen app (a video, a game), the island hidden again between them. Off, they wait until the app leaves full screen, as GNOME's own.

"primary": the main display, in its top bar. "active": the display of the window in use; on a display without a top bar it hangs from the top edge. "all": every display, the island itself on the one in use; the others show the closed island and its alerts, and pointing at one brings the island there.
How far the closed island hangs below the top bar, in pixels, when it is not inside the top bar.

With the closed island inside the top bar: the top bar is a little taller than the island, so the island stops just short of the windows below. Off, they are the same height. It shows on a see-through or grey bar.

Show battery, network, Bluetooth and Caps Lock alerts
help: Before 0.7, one switch for all four; now each has its own (alert-power, alert-network, alert-bluetooth, alert-caps-lock), and this one is only read once to carry an "off" over.

item: Alert when a Bluetooth device's battery is low
help: At 20, 10 and 5 percent, once per level on the way down, for each connected device that reports its battery; again once it has charged more than 5 points above that level. Like the laptop's low battery, it shows during Do Not Disturb. Off until you turn it on.
An alert before each event with a time, with a Join button when it has a meeting link.

item: Minutes before an event its alert shows
World clocks on the Calendar page
help: A globe on the Calendar page shows the time in the cities of GNOME’s World Clocks.

item: Pages left out of the island
help: Names of the open island’s pages that have no tab: music, notifications, focus, reminders, shelf, calendar. The Apps and Usage pages have their own switches (app-usage, usage-enabled).

item: The Apps page, timing the application in front
help: Shows the Apps page and times the application in front, whether or not there is keyboard or pointer input, keeping 30 days on this computer. Time pauses after five idle minutes, unless a video or another program holds the session awake. Off until you turn it on; off, nothing is timed and the page has no tab.
Shows the Devices page: each connected Bluetooth device with its battery. Its tab shows only while a device is connected. Off until you turn it on.

item: Answer Claude Code from the island
help: When on, Island adds a hook to Claude Code's settings so it hears when Claude needs you or is done; off removes it.
When on, Island adds hooks to Codex's hooks.json so it hears when Codex needs you or is done; off removes them.

item: Leave notifications to GNOME's own banners
help: The island then shows no notification alerts; its Notifications page still lists them.

"island": the island's clipboard history. "calendar": the island's Calendar page. "none": nothing. "gnome" is from before and reads as "calendar". With that page left out of the island, it opens the other one. It is GNOME's own shortcut (Super+V and Super+M), so Island adds none.

item: How long the assistant keeps a conversation
help: Until midnight (never more than a day), or after 30 minutes or 2 hours without a word: then it starts a new one and deletes the old, here and in the AI's own history.
